title: Console metric discovery and incident replay runbook
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Summary: During a recent production capacity regression (2026-02-10) the Console hit a degradation path that was not well covered by our telemetry. Aggregated dashboards masked per-route tail latency increases; several ingress queues were saturated with no surfaced queue-depth or backpressure metrics; KV cache evictions were visible only in sporadic logs and not as structured spans. This ticket creates a prioritized discovery sweep to catalog missing signals, implements lightweight incident replay tooling to reproduce surge patterns against staging, and codifies an on-call runbook + dashboard changes to prevent recurrence.
steps: Inventory current Console telemetry: list dashboards, panels, traced spans, and raw metrics mapped to request path and tenant
Define a gap catalog: for each missing signal (queue depth, per-tenant tail latency, KV eviction counters, prefix-cache hit/miss by tenant) add priority and owner
Add compact heartbeat metrics for key subsystems (ingress-queue-depth, batch-queue-latency, kv-evictions-per-minute, route-token-throughput) with 1s/5s resolution for emergencies
Create incident-replay harness: small tool to replay captured ingress patterns (RPS, small/large requests, KV-hot prefixes) to staging and record dashboards/traces
Refactor top-level Console dashboards: replace opaque rollups with selectable aggregation (global/tenant/route) and per-route p50/p95/p99 panels
Instrument missing trace spans: attach KV cache eviction spans and ingress queue lifecycle spans with correlation_id that ties to Console request id
Add alerts and escalation flow: SLO breach + queue-depth > threshold => on-call paging with runbook checklist
Publish runbook and run tabletop incident drill with SRE and Console product owners
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Console PM and infra eng done. Agreed on initial signal list and owners.
2026-02-20: Lightweight heartbeat metrics PoC merged (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/214). Metrics exposed under console.ingress.* and console.kv.* with 5s scrape.
2026-02-25: Incident-replay prototype created; replayed 10k RPS burst in staging and captured missing queue-depth signals. Finding: sampling configuration drops spans when request latency > 250ms.
2026-03-01: Dashboard proposal reviewed by Console PM and UX; agreed to add a tenant selector and split p99 from aggregated p95. UX work queued as DES-2102.
2026-03-03: Tracing change merged that adds kv_eviction and ingress_queue spans (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/987). Next: validate end-to-end correlation in staging runs.
acceptance_criteria: All high-priority gaps in the gap catalog have an assigned owner and an implementation plan
Heartbeat metrics are in production and are visible in Console overview with 5s resolution
Incident-replay tool can reproduce the 2026-02-10 regression in staging reliably and produces comparable dashboard/traces
Dashboards allow filtering by tenant and display p50/p95/p99 for chosen routes
Tracing surfaces kv_eviction and ingress_queue spans correlated with request IDs and token counts
On-call runbook published and validated via tabletop drill with SRE and Console PM
risks: Increasing metric cardinality could raise storage and query cost if full-tenant tags are enabled; mitigation: start with sampled tenant IDs for top 5 tenants and use rollups for others
Span volume spike from added tracing could increase ingest; mitigation: use dynamic sampling thresholds during healthy vs degraded states
Replay harness may not perfectly simulate cross-service backpressure; mitigation: include simple downstream latency injection knobs and KV cache warm/cold modes
